actions.description: Advance the simulated world by a bounded number of fixed timesteps, optionally applying an action for each step, and return the resulting observation and terminal flags.

inputs.description: Transitions to advance; the action is applied at every tick
inputs.name: ticks

inputs.description: The action applied at each tick, shaped by the environment's action space

actions.description: Reset the simulated world to a scenario start state and return the initial observation. When a seed is supplied the endpoint records it in the receipt; otherwise the endpoint's declared default seed applies.

inputs.description: Accepted for the class contract; a MuJoCo reset restores the model defaults (mj_resetData) and does not use a seed

facts.text: PolySim is a whole-body-control training platform that integrates multiple heterogeneous simulators
The TODO list marks sim2sim in MuJoCo released and sim2real videos with the Unitree SDK on G1 still unchecked
The MuJoCo environment section installs mujoco and torch with pip
The MuJoCo simulator config sets _target_ to humanoidverse.simulator.mujoco.mujoco.MuJoCo, the simulator name to mujoco, fps 200, control_decimation 4, substeps 1 and gravity 0 0 -9.81
setup derives sim_dt as 1 / sim.fps and sim_substeps from sim.substeps
load_assets loads the MJCF with mujoco.MjModel.from_xml_path, overwrites opt.timestep with 0.005 s and constructs an MjData
The simulation loop writes the PD torques to data.ctrl and calls mujoco.mj_step
The scene declares the model g1_29dof scene and includes g1_29dof_old.xml
The included model declares g1_29dof and the compiler angle unit radian with meshdir meshes
The world body pelvis starts at 0 0 0.793 and carries the free joint floating_base_joint
The actuator section has 29 motor actuators, one per hinge joint, each with an explicit ctrlrange

The control ranges are -88 88 for the hips and waist yaw, -139 139 for the knees, -50 50 for the ankles and waist roll/pitch, -25 25 for the shoulders, elbows and wrist rolls, and -5 5 for wrist pitch/yaw
The Sim2Sim config points ROBOT_SCENE at ../humanoidverse/data/robots/g1/scene_29dof.xml

determinism.notes: MuJoCo integrates the fixed model deterministically from the model defaults; the bridge accepts a seed in cap.world.reset.v1 but a MuJoCo reset restores the model defaults and does not use it, so one control sequence repeats a trajectory on the same engine.  The package's stand-in is deterministic too, but its placeholder motion is not the engine's physics.

gaps: the fake backend is a stand-in for the mujoco library, not MuJoCo: it parses the MJCF for the free base, the 29 hinge joints, the 29 motor actuators, their explicit ctrlranges and the included model file, then gives each actuated hinge a placeholder velocity proportional to its control value and holds the free base where the model puts it; it computes no inertia, torque, gravity, contact, friction, constraint, damping or actuator dynamics and produces no MuJoCo trajectory
the stand-in loads no STL mesh or texture and resolves no collision or contact; the model's floor, collision geoms, sites, sensors and default classes are parsed only for the joint and actuator shape

the scene and the included robot model declare no <option timestep>; the stand-in therefore reports a placeholder default step, while the upstream simulator overwrites model.opt.timestep with 0.005 s after loading (mujoco.py:148) and its own setup uses 1/fps (mujoco.py:57, fps 200 in mujoco.yaml:15); this package loads the MJCF directly and does not run that loop

the upstream class humanoidverse.simulator.mujoco.mujoco:MuJoCo needs Hydra, Torch and a viewer and is not imported or run by this package; its control loop, terrain setup and sensors are not exposed here
the fake reset restores the parsed model qpos0 and zeros; a real MjData reset also restores the full integration state, which this package did not inspect
MuJoCo itself was not importable where the gate ran, so no trajectory of this package was compared with the real engine
no physical G1 is modelled and nothing was validated against the Unitree hardware
